The '''2019–20 Barcelona season''' was [[FC Barcelona|the club]]'s [[List of FC Barcelona seasons|121st season]] in existence and the [[All-time La Liga table|89th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football. Barcelona competed in [[2019–20 La Liga|La Liga]], the [[2019–20 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], the [[2019 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] and the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. The season covered the period from 1 July 2019 to 14 August 2020.

The club endured its worst season in years, going trophyless for the first time since [[2007–08 FC Barcelona season|2007–08]]. Head coach [[Ernesto Valverde]] was replaced by [[Quique Setién]] in January 2020 after a Supercopa defeat to [[Atlético Madrid]], but that did not improve the team's fortunes, as they lost the closely fought title race to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and were [[FC Barcelona 2–8 FC Bayern Munich|defeated 8–2]] by [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in a one-legged Champions League quarter-final tie.

==Season overview==
{{cleanup|section|reason=a single-sentence description of every single game, with no summary or context, has very little value|date=July 2026}}
[[File:Only dictatorships jail peaceful political leaders Barcelona Inter.jpeg|thumb|The opening ceremony for FC Barcelona vs. Inter game in Camp Nou, Barcelona.]]

===June===
On 26 June, [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] announced the departure of [[Jasper Cillessen]] to [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] for a fee of €35 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1256990/agreement-with-valencia-for-transfer-of-jasper-cillessen |title=Agreement with Valencia for transfer of Jasper Cillessen |date=26 June 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=11 July 2019}}</ref> The following day on 27 June, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Neto (footballer, born 1989)|Neto]] from Valencia for a fee of €26 million plus €9 million in add-ons.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1257005/agreement-with-valencia-for-transfer-of-norberto-murara-neto |title=Agreement with Valencia for transfer of Norberto Murara 'Neto' |date=27 June 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=11 July 2019}}</ref>

On 30 June, [[Denis Suárez]] was sold to [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] for €12.9 million plus €3.1 million in add-ons.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1259963/agreement-with-celta-for-the-transfer-of-denis-suarez |title=Agreement with Celta for the transfer of Denis Suárez |date=30 June 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=11 July 2019}}</ref>

===July===
On 3 July, the Vice President of Sports Jordi Mestre resigned.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1263896/fc-barcelona-communique |title=FC Barcelona communiqué |date=3 July 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=11 July 2019}}</ref>

On 12 July, Barcelona signed [[Antoine Griezmann]] from [[Atlético Madrid]] after triggering his €120,000,000 buyout clause.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1277948/barca-sign-antoine-griezmann |title=Barça sign Antoine Griezmann |date=12 July 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 July 2019}}</ref> Barcelona also sold [[Adrián Ortolá]] to [[CD Tenerife]] for an undisclosed price.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1278166/agreement-with-cd-tenerife-for-transfer-of-adrian-ortola |title=Agreement with CD Tenerife for transfer of Adrián Ortolá |date=12 July 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 July 2019}}</ref>

On 16 July, Barcelona activated [[Marc Cucurella]]'s buy-back clause of €4 million, only two months after [[SD Eibar|Eibar]] had permanently signed him for €2 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1280408/barca-activate-cucurella-buy-back-clause |title=Barça activate Cucurella buy-back clause |date=16 July 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=17 July 2019}}</ref>

On 18 July, Barcelona and [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] reached an agreement for the loan of Cucurella to the Madrid side for the rest of the season with an option to buy for €6 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1288455/agreement-with-getafe-for-the-loan-of-marc-cucurella |title=Agreement with Getafe for the loan of Marc Cucurella |date=18 July 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=21 July 2019}}</ref>

===August===
On 2 August, Barça and [[Russian Premier League]] club [[FC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit St Petersburg]] agreed to the transfer of [[Malcom (footballer)|Malcom]] for a fee of €45,000,000 plus variables.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1299288/agreement-with-zenit-saint-petersburg-for-the-transfer-of-malcom/ |title=Agreement with Zenit St Petersburg for the transfer of Malcom. |date=2 August 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=3 August 2019}}</ref>

On 4 August, Barça and [[Real Betis]] reached an agreement for the signing of [[Junior Firpo]] for €18 million plus €12 million in variables.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1300141/barca-sign-junior-firpo# |title=Barça sign Junior Firpo |date=4 August 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=22 August 2019}}</ref>

On 16 August, Barça started their season in a 0–1 away defeat to [[Athletic Bilbao]] from a late winner from [[Aritz Aduriz]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1313365/athletic-club-fc-barcelona-out-of-luck-1-0 |title=Athletic Club – FC Barcelona: Out of luck (1-0) |date=16 August 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=22 August 2019}}</ref>

On 18 August, Barça and [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] reached an agreement for the loan of [[Philippe Coutinho]] to the German side for the rest of the season with an option to buy for €120 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1313389/agreement-with-bayern-munich-for-philippe-coutinho-loan |title=Agreement with Bayern Munich for Philippe Coutinho loan |date=19 August 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=22 August 2019}}</ref>

On 25 August, Barça defeated Real Betis in a 5–2 home rout, goals from Antoine Griezmann, [[Carles Pérez]], [[Jordi Alba]], and [[Arturo Vidal]] led the ''Blaugrana'' to victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1326338/barca-52-betis-five-star |title=Barça 5–2 Betis: Five-star! |date=25 August 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=28 August 2019}}</ref>

On 31 August, Barça drew 2–2 away at [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] with goals from [[Ansu Fati]] and [[Arthur Melo|Arthur]], with the forward becoming the youngest player in FC Barcelona's history to score a goal in La Liga (16 years and 304 days).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1332644/osasuna-22-barca-a-point-in-pamplona |title=Osasuna 2–2 Barça: A point in Pamplona |date=31 August 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=4 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1332598/ansu-fati-becomes-youngest-ever-fc-barcelona-goalscorer-in-la-liga |title=Ansu Fati becomes youngest ever FC Barcelona goalscorer in La Liga |date=31 August 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=4 September 2019}}</ref>

===September===
On 2 September, [[Rafinha (footballer, born February 1993)|Rafinha]] extended his contract by one year until 2021 and moved to Celta Vigo on loan for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1335462/rafinha-extends-deal-with-barca-goes-to-celta-on-loan |title=Rafinha extends deal with Barça, goes to Celta on loan |date=2 September 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=4 September 2019}}</ref>

On September 14, Barça defeated Valencia in a 5−2 win at home. Goals from Ansu Fati, [[Frenkie de Jong]], [[Gerard Piqué]], and a brace from [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] once again led the ''Blaugrana'' to victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1345583/fc-barcelona-5-2-valencia-wow |title=FC Barcelona 5-2 Valencia: Wow! |date=14 September 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=26 September 2019}}</ref>

On 17 September, Barça started their [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|Champions League campaign]] with a 0−0 away draw with [[Borussia Dortmund]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1348413/borussia-dortmund-0-0-barca-a-point-to-start-with |title=Borussia Dortmund 0-0 Barça: A point to start with |date=17 September 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=26 September 2019}}</ref>

On 21 September, Barça suffered a 2−0 away loss to [[Granada CF]], conceding goals from [[Antonio Puertas]] and [[Álvaro Vadillo]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1353544/granada-2-0-fc-barcelona-beaten-in-andalusia |title=Granada 2-0 FC Barcelona: Beaten in Andalusia |date=21 September 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=26 September 2019}}</ref>

On 24 September, Barça defeated [[Villarreal CF]] 2−1 at home. First half goals from Antoine Griezmann and Arthur were enough for the home side to claim victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1357370/fc-barcelona-2-1-villarreal-job-done-at-camp-nou |title=FC Barcelona 2-1 Villarreal: Job done at Camp Nou |date=24 September 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=26 September 2019}}</ref>

On 28 September, Barça defeated [[Getafe CF]] 2–0 away from home. Luis Suárez and Junior Firpo got themselves on the score sheet.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1361708/getafe-cf-02-fc-barcelona-a-capital-victory |title=Getafe CF 0–2 FC Barcelona: A capital victory |date=28 September 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 October 2019}}</ref> Clemént Lenglet got sent off and received his first red card of the season.

===October===
On 2 October, Barça defeated [[Inter Milan]] 2–1 at home in the UEFA Champions League. Inter scored early through [[Lautaro Martínez]] but Barça came-back after Luis Suárez scored twice to earn the victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1367050/barca-2-1-inter-milan-spirited-fightback |title=Barça 2-1 Inter Milan: Spirited fightback |date=2 October 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 October 2019}}</ref>

On 6 October, Barça defeated [[Sevilla FC]] 4–0 at home. Luis Suárez, Arturo Vidal, [[Ousmane Dembélé]] and [[Lionel Messi]] (both with their first goals of the season) lead the ''Blaugrana'' to victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1373160/fc-barcelona-4-0-sevilla-a-thriller-at-camp-nou |title=FC Barcelona 4-0 Sevilla: A thriller at Camp Nou |date=6 October 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 October 2019}}</ref> Both Dembélé and [[Ronald Araújo]] got sent off.

On 19 October, Barça defeated [[SD Eibar]] 3–0 away from home. Goals from Antoine Griezmann, Lionel Messi, and Luis Suárez helped the Blaugrana extend their winning run to five games.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1456777/sd-eibar-0-3-barca-winning-run-continues |title=SD Eibar 0-3 Barça: Winning run continues |date=19 October 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 November 2019}}</ref>

On 23 October, Barça defeated [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]] in the UEFA Champions League 2–1 away from home. Goals coming in from Lionel Messi and a [[Peter Olayinka]] own goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1464539/slavia-prague-1-2-barca-solid-in-europe |title=Slavia Prague 1-2 Barça: Solid in Europe |date=23 October 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 November 2019}}</ref>

On 29 October, Barça defeated [[Real Valladolid]] 5–1 at home with goals from Clément Lenglet, Arturo Vidal, a brace from Messi and a goal from Suárez giving Barcelona seven straight wins.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1474724/five-goal-masterclass-5-1 |title=Five-goal masterclass (5-1) |date=29 October 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 November 2019}}</ref>

===November===
On 2 November, Barcelona lost to [[Levante UD|Levante]] 3–1 away from home. A penalty converted by Messi gave the ''Blaugrana'' the lead in the first half but 3 goals in 7 minutes during the second half handed the home side the victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1479460/levante-3-1-barca-winning-run-comes-to-an-end |title=Levante 3-1 Barça: Winning run comes to an end |date=2 November 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 November 2019}}</ref>

On 5 November, Barcelona drew 0–0 with Slavia Prague in the UEFA Champions League at home.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1483813/fc-barcelona-0-0-slavia-prague-goalless-at-camp-nou |title=FC Barcelona 0-0 Slavia Prague: Goalless at Camp Nou |date=5 November 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 November 2019}}</ref>

On 9 November, Barcelona defeated Celta Vigo 4–1 at home. Lionel Messi scored his first [[hat-trick]] of the season and [[Sergio Busquets]] scored one.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1490878/four-midable |title=Four-midable! |date=9 November 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

On 23 November, Barcelona narrowly defeated [[CD Leganés|Leganés]] 2–1. Goals from Luis Suárez and Arturo Vidal cancelled out [[Youssef En-Nesyri]]'s earlier goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1500535/barca-and-their-supersubs |title=Barça and their supersubs |date=23 November 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

On 27 November, Barcelona defeated Borussia Dortmund 3–1 in the UEFA Champions League, securing a spot in the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|round of 16]] and finishing as group winners. Lionel Messi, Luis Suárez, and Antoine Griezmann were the goalscorers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1506359/barca-3-1-borussia-dortmund-wunderbarca |title=Barça 3-1 Borussia Dortmund: WunderBarça! |date=27 November 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

===December===
On 1 December, Barcelona defeated Atlético Madrid 1–0 away from home. Messi scored five minutes from time at the [[Wanda Metropolitano]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1512583/atletico-0-1-barca-wanda-win |title=Atlético 0-1 Barça: Wanda win!|date=1 December 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

On 7 December, Barcelona defeated [[RCD Mallorca|Real Mallorca]] 5–2 at home. Messi scored his second hat-trick of the season, while Griezmann and Suárez also appeared on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1522587/fc-barcelona-5-2-mallorca-golden-football |title=FC Barcelona 5-2 Mallorca: Golden football |date=7 December 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

On 10 December, a rotated Barcelona team defeated Inter Milan 2–1 away from home in the UEFA Champions League. Carles Pérez and Ansu Fati scored, the latter making history by becoming the youngest goalscorer in the history competition.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1526646/inter-milan-1-2-barca-veni-vidi-vici |title=Inter Milan 1-2 Barça: Veni, vidi, vici! |date=10 December 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=17 January 2020}}</ref>

On 14 December, Barcelona drew 2–2 away at [[Real Sociedad]]. Antoine Griezmann scored against his old club, while Luis Suárez scored the second.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1533169/real-sociedad-2-2-fc-barcelona-points-shared-in-san-sebastian |title=Real Sociedad 2-2 FC Barcelona: Points shared in San Sebastián |date=14 December 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

On 18 December, Barcelona drew 0–0 against rivals [[Real Madrid]] in [[El Clásico]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1537900/fc-barcelona-0-0-real-madrid-high-drama-no-goals |title=FC Barcelona 0-0 Real Madrid: High drama, no goals |date=18 December 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref> It became the first time in over 17 years that both rivals ended goalless in the league, the last time being during the [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03]] season.<ref>[https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/barcelona-vs-real-madrid-result-final-score-clasico-gareth-bale-goal-lionel-messi-a9252711.html Barcelona vs Real Madrid result: El Clasico makes history for wrong reasons as La Liga leaders play out rare draw]; ''[[The Independent]]''. 19 December 2019</ref>

On 21 December, Barcelona defeated [[Deportivo Alavés]] 4–1 at home in the last game of the year. Griezmann, Arturo Vidal, Messi, and Suárez all scored. The Uruguayan was involved in all 4 goals, contributing 1 goal and 3 assists.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1541330/fc-barcelona-4-1-alaves-winning-end-to-2019 |title=FC Barcelona 4-1 Alavés: Winning end to 2019 |date=21 December 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

On 28 December, Barcelona and Real Betis reached an agreement for the loan of [[Carles Aleñá]] for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1550008/agreement-with-betis-for-the-loan-of-carles-alena# |title=Agreement with Betis for the loan of Carles Aleñá |date=28 December 2019 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=17 July 2020}}</ref>

===January===
On 4 January, Barcelona drew 2–2 with local rivals [[RCD Espanyol]] in the ''[[Derbi barceloní|Barcelona derby]]''. The ''Blaugrana'' conceded early when [[David López (footballer, born 1989)|David López]] nodded in a free kick but Barça made a comeback with goals from Luis Suárez and Arturo Vidal. Espanyol drew late with a goal from [[Wu Lei]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1561711/espanyol-2-2-barca-derby-point |title=Espanyol 2-2 Barça: Derby point |date=4 January 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

On 9 January, Barcelona were knocked out of the [[2019–20 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] after being defeated 3–2 to Atlético Madrid.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1565210/barca-2-3-atletico-madrid-late-drama-ends-super-cup-hopes |title=Barça 2-3 Atlético Madrid: Late drama ends Super Cup hopes |date=9 January 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

On 13 January, Barcelona terminated [[Ernesto Valverde]]'s contract after two and a half seasons in charge. The club appointed [[Quique Setién]] as the new head coach until 30 June 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1571123/agreement-for-the-termination-of-ernesto-valverdes-contract |title=Agreement for the termination of Ernesto Valverde's contract |date=13 January 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1571121/quique-setien-is-the-new-coach-of-fc-barcelona |title=Quique Setién is the new coach of FC Barcelona |date=13 January 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

On 15 January, Barcelona reached an agreement with [[FC Schalke 04]] for the loan on [[Jean-Clair Todibo]] for the remainder of the season. The German side paid a €1.5 million loan fee and obtained a buy option for €25 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news# |title=Agreement with Schalke 04 for Todibo on loan |date=15 January 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=17 January 2020}}</ref>

On 19 January, Barcelona defeated Granada 1–0 at home. A second half goal from Messi saw Quique Setién win his first game in charge as a Barça coach.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1579842/barca-1-0-granada-solid-start-for-setien |title=Barça 1-0 Granada: Solid start for Setién |date=19 January 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=19 January 2020}}</ref>

On 22 January, Barcelona defeated [[UD Ibiza]] 2–1 away from home in the [[Copa del Rey]]. Ibiza scored first, but an Antoine Griezmann brace secured a comeback for the ''Blaugrana''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1584989/ud-ibiza-12-barca-copa-comeback |title=UD Ibiza 1–2 Barça: Copa comeback! |date=22 January 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 February 2020}}</ref>

On 25 January, Barcelona lost 2–0 to Valencia away from home. A brace from [[Maxi Gómez]] sealed a victory for ''Los Che''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1589246/valencia-2-0-fc-barcelona-a-tough-loss |title=Valencia 2-0 FC Barcelona: A tough loss |date=25 January 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 February 2020}}</ref>

On 30 January, Barcelona defeated Leganés 5–0 at home in the Copa del Rey. Goals from Antoine Griezmann, Clément Lenglet, Arthur and a Leo Messi brace gave Barça a passage into the next round.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1594337/five-star-performance |title=Five star performance |date=30 January 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 February 2020}}</ref>

On 31 January, Barcelona reached an agreement with [[OGC Nice]] for the loan of [[Moussa Wagué]] for the remainder of the season. The French side obtained a buy option for €10 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1595379/agreement-with-ogc-nice-for-the-loan-transfer-of-wague# |title=Agreement with OGC Nice for the loan transfer of Wague |date=31 January 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=17 July 2020}}</ref>

===February===
On 2 February, Barcelona defeated Levante 2–1 at home in the league. A brace from Ansu Fati gave Barça the win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1600875/barca-21-levante-double-delight |title=Barça 2–1 Levante: Double delight! |date=2 February 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=9 February 2020}}</ref>

On 6 February, Barcelona were eliminated from the [[2019–20 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] by Athletic Bilbao in the quarter-finals. A late [[Iñaki Williams]] header secured a passage for the home side into the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1603993/injury-time-ko-1-0 |title=Injury time KO (1-0) |date=6 February 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=9 February 2020}}</ref>

On 9 February, Barcelona defeated Real Betis 3–2 away from home. Goals from [[Sergio Canales]] and [[Nabil Fekir]] weren't enough for the home side as de Jong, Busquets and Lenglet scored for the away team. Messi assisted all three goals and Lenglet received a second yellow card, getting sent off.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1606770/betis-23-barca-thriller-at-the-villamarin |title=Betis 2–3 Barça: Thriller at the Villamarín |date=9 February 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref>

On 15 February, Barcelona defeated Getafe 2–1 at home. Antoine Griezmann and [[Sergi Roberto]] scored, but Barça conceded a consolation from [[Ángel Rodríguez (footballer, born 1987)|Ángel Rodríguez]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1610968/barca-getafe-home-sweet-home-2-1 |title=Barça – Getafe: Home sweet home! (2-1) |date=15 February 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref>

On 20 February, Barcelona signed [[Martin Braithwaite]] from Leganés for €18 million. Barcelona was given permission from La Liga to sign an emergency forward as Luis Suárez and Ousmane Dembélé were both ruled out with injuries for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1615162/fc-barcelona-sign-martin-braithwaite |title=FC Barcelona sign Martin Braithwaite |date=20 February 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref><ref>[https://en.as.com/en/2020/02/19/football/1582133734_349797.html Barcelona to sign Braithwaite as Dembélé cover] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413085028/https://en.as.com/en/2020/02/19/football/1582133734_349797.html |date=13 April 2021 }}; ''[[Diario AS]]''  20 February 2020</ref>

On 22 February, Barcelona defeated Eibar 5–0  at home. Messi scored a first half hat-trick and scored once again late on. Arthur also scored.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1619352/barca-5-0-eibar-messi-masterclass |title=Barça 5-0 Eibar: Messi masterclass! |date=22 February 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref>

On 25 February, Barcelona drew 1–1 with [[S.S.C. Napoli]] in the first leg of their [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League#Round of 16|UEFA Champions League round of 16 tie]]. Antoine Griezmann cancelled out [[Dries Mertens]]' opener in Naples.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1624953/napoli-1-1-barca-all-to-be-decided-at-camp-nou |title=Napoli 1-1 Barça: All to be decided at Camp Nou |date=25 February 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref>

===March===
On 1 March, Barcelona lost 2–0 to bitter rivals Real Madrid away from home, making it the first time since 25 October 2014 that Barcelona lost at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] in league play. It was Setién's first Clásico as a Barça coach since taking charge in January.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1632750/real-madrid-2-0-fc-barcelona-beaten-at-the-bernabeu |title=Real Madrid 2-0 FC Barcelona: Beaten at the Bernabéu |date=1 March 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=6 May 2020}}</ref>

On 7 March, Barcelona defeated Real Sociedad 1–0 at home after Lionel Messi converted a late penalty.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1639990/barca-10-real-sociedad-back-to-winning-ways |title=Barça 1–0 Real Sociedad: Back to winning ways |date=7 March 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=6 May 2020}}</ref>

On 12 March, the next two league matchdays were suspended to combat the spread of [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1644711/next-two-laliga-matchdays-suspended |title=Next two LaLiga matchdays suspended |date=12 March 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=6 May 2020}}</ref>

On 13 March, the club suspended all first team activity until further notice.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1645243/fc-barcelona-first-team-suspends-all-activity |title=FC Barcelona first team suspends all activity |date=13 March 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=6 May 2020}}</ref>

On 23 March, La Liga was suspended indefinitely due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/coronavirus-laliga-suspended-indefinitely/1759ghuyenand1ws6gkns0we9z |title=La Liga 2019-2020 season suspended indefinitely due to coronavirus |date=23 March 2020 |publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]] |access-date=6 May 2020}}</ref>

===June===
On 13 June, after a three-month hiatus, Barcelona returned to action against Real Mallorca away from home. Barcelona won 4–0 behind closed doors. Arturo Vidal, Martin Braithwaite, Jordi Alba and Messi scored for the ''Blaugrana''. Braithwaite also scored his first goal as a Barça player.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1681653/mallorca-0-4-barca-back-with-a-bang |title=Mallorca 0-4 Barça: Back with a bang |date=13 June 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=16 June 2020}}</ref>

On 16 June, Barcelona defeated Leganés 2–0 at home. Ansu Fati and Messi scored.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1683065/victorious-homecoming-2-0 |title=Victorious homecoming (2-0) |date=16 June 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=18 June 2020}}</ref>

On 19 June, Barcelona drew 0–0 away against Sevilla.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1686784/no-goals-but-a-hard-earned-point |title=No goals, but a hard-earned point |date=19 June 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=21 June 2020}}</ref>

On 23 June, Barcelona defeated Athletic Bilbao 1–0 at home. [[Ivan Rakitić]] came off to bench to score his first goal of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1694654/barca-1-0-athletic-one-goal-three-points |title=Barça 1-0 Athletic: One goal, three points |date=23 June 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=24 June 2020}}</ref>

On 27 June, Barcelona drew 2–2 away against Celta Vigo. Luis Suárez scored twice for the visitors and [[Fyodor Smolov]] and [[Iago Aspas]] scored for the home side.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1700077/celta-2-2-barca-twice-ahead-but-points-shared |title=Celta 2-2 Barça: Twice ahead, but points shared |date=27 June 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=28 June 2020}}</ref>

On 29 June, Barcelona and [[Juventus F.C.|Juventus]] reached an agreement over the transfer of Arthur for a fee of €72 million plus €10 million in variables. The club also confirmed the signing of [[Miralem Pjanić]] from Juventus for a fee of €60 million plus €5 million in variables. Arthur and Pjanić will join their respective clubs once the season concludes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1700293/agreement-with-juventus-for-the-transfer-of-arthur# |title=Agreement with Juventus for the transfer of Arthur |date=29 June 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=29 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1700297/fc-barcelona-sign-miralem-pjanic# |title=FC Barcelona sign Miralem Pjanić |date=29 June 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=29 June 2020}}</ref>

On 30 June, Getafe triggered Marc Cucurella's option to buy for €10 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1702077/getafe-exercise-option-to-purchase-marc-cucurella |title=Getafe exercise option to purchase Marc Cucurella |date=30 June 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=30 June 2020}}</ref> On the same day Barça faced Atlético Madrid at home. The Catalans took the lead through a [[Diego Costa]] [[own goal]] but Atlético equalized with a controversial penalty, converted by [[Saúl (footballer, born 1994)|Saúl]]. Barcelona took the lead through another controversial penalty decision and Messi converted his 700th career goal, but Atlético equalized once again with another questionable penalty decision, with Saúl scoring again from the spot.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1702850/barca-2-2-atletico-madrid-another-cruel-draw |title=Barça 2-2 Atlético Madrid: Another cruel draw |date=30 June 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref>

===July===
On 5 July, Barcelona defeated Villarreal 4–1 away from home. Goals from Suárez, Griezmann, Fati, and a [[Pau Torres (footballer, born 1997)|Pau Torres]] own goal gave Barça the win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1712138/villarreal-1-4-barca-thriller-at-villarreal |title=Villarreal 1-4 Barça: Thriller at Villarreal |date=5 July 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=6 July 2020}}</ref>

On 8 July, Barcelona defeated local rivals Espanyol 1–0 at home, relegating them to the [[Segunda División]] in the process. Suárez scored his 195th goal, overtaking [[László Kubala]] as the club's [[List of FC Barcelona records and statistics#Top goalscorers|third top all-time goalscorer]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1716927/fc-barcelona-1-0-espanyol-job-done |title=FC Barcelona 1-0 Espanyol: Job done |date=8 July 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref>

On 11 July, Barcelona defeated Real Valladolid 1–0 away from home. Arturo Vidal scored the only goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1721683/valladolid-0-1-fc-barcelona-still-in-contention |title=Valladolid 0-1 FC Barcelona: Still in contention |date=11 July 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=12 July 2020}}</ref>

On 16 July, Barcelona lost to Osasuna 2–1 at home. Former Barça player [[José Arnaiz]] and [[Roberto Torres (footballer, born 1989)|Roberto Torres]] scored for the visitors, while Messi scored the only goal for the home side.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1729084/fc-barcelona-1-2-osasuna-la-liga-slips-away# |title=FC Barcelona 1-2 Osasuna: La Liga slips away |date=16 July 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=16 July 2020}}</ref> In the same day, rivals Real Madrid claimed the [[2019–20 La Liga|La Liga title]] in a 2–1 victory against Villarreal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2020/07/16/football/real-madrid-villarreal-zinedine-zidane-wins-la-liga-spt-intl/index.html |title=Real Madrid crowned La Liga champion for first time since 2017 with victory over Villarreal |date=16 July 2020 |publisher=[[CNN]] |access-date=16 July 2020}}</ref>

On 19 July, Barcelona ended the league season by defeating Alavés 5–0 away from home. Messi scored a brace, Fati, Suárez and [[Nélson Semedo]] – with his first of the season – also scored.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1732746/alaves-0-5-fc-barcelona-ending-on-a-high# |title=Alavés 0-5 FC Barcelona: Ending on a high |date=19 July 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=19 July 2020}}</ref>

===August===
On 8 August, Barcelona defeated Napoli 3–1 at home in the second leg of their [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League#Round of 16|UEFA Champions League round of 16 tie]]. Lenglet, Messi, and Suárez scored.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1750427/fc-barcelona-3-1-napoli-lisbon-here-we-come |title=FC Barcelona 3-1 Napoli: Lisbon here we come! |date=8 August 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 August 2020}}</ref>

On 14 August, Barcelona's season ended after losing [[FC Barcelona 2–8 FC Bayern Munich|8–2]] to Bayern Munich in the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League#Quarter-finals|UEFA Champions League single-leg quarter-final]]. [[Thomas Müller]] and Barça loanee Philippe Coutinho scored twice, while [[Ivan Perišić]], [[Serge Gnabry]], [[Joshua Kimmich]], and [[Robert Lewandowski]] all scored one goal each. [[David Alaba]] scored an own goal for the ''Blaugrana'' and Suárez scored.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1753729/barca-2-8-bayern-painful-exit-from-europe |title=Barça 2-8 Bayern: Painful exit from Europe |date=14 August 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=15 August 2020}}</ref> The loss was the biggest defeat in history in a UEFA Champions League knockout match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/manuelveth/2020/08/14/bayern-munich-write-history-in-8-2-victory-over-barcelona/#19fdcb4dd52d |title=Bayern Munich Write History In 8-2 Victory Over Barcelona |date=14 August 2020 |work=[[Forbes]] |access-date=15 August 2020}}</ref>
